title: Bias Dynamics in BabyLMs: Towards a Compute-Efficient Sandbox for Democratising Pre-Training Debiasing
findings: The analysis of training corpora found that Christian terms dominate in both the BabyLM and BERT corpora, while Jewish terms are barely represented. The BERT corpus contained a substantially higher frequency of Muslim terms compared to the BabyLM corpus. Overall, the BabyLM corpus largely preserved similar topic ratios for religious groups as the larger BERT corpus, indicating it could support similar debiasing experiments. Sentiment analysis showed both corpora had negative sentiment stances towards Jewish and Muslim topics, with BERT being more negative.

measurement_description: The frequency of religious demographic terms (Christian, Muslim, Jewish) within the training corpora (BabyLM and a reconstructed BERT corpus), and the sentiment of sentences containing these terms. This was part of a broader analysis to establish whether compact models (BabyLMs) can serve as proxies for larger models in bias research.
